newsitem.title: USA: FOMC voted 11-1 for steady rates at Sep 24 meeting.
newsitem.headline: FOMC voted 11-1 for steady rates at Sep 24 meeting.

text.p: The Federal Reserve's policy-making body voted 11-1 at its Sept. 24 meeting to keep short-term U.S. interest rates steady and maintained its bias toward tighter credit, according to minutes of the meeting released Friday.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) again elected to keep interest rates unchanged at its most recent meeting Wednesday. However, the minutes of that meeting will not be made public until late December.
In the September session, Minneapolis Fed President Gary Stern dissented for the third time in a row in favour of an immediate interest rate hike, the minutes show.
"Given prevailing pressures on resources, especially labour, Mr. Stern was concerned about the distinct risk of an acceleration in inflation," according to the minutes.
"A few" of Stern's colleagues were willing to vote for higher rates, but they "did not feel any urgency about such a move," the minutes show.
As a whole, the FOMC members generally agreed that inflation was more likely to rise than fall.

"The members generally agreed that while the risks were greater that price inflation would rise than that it would fall, higher inflation was not a foregone conclusion and most believed ... it prudent to hold monetary policy on a steady course and await further developments," the minutes read.
The Fed staff forecast prepared for the September FOMC meeting showed the U.S. economic expansion slowing to a rate "around, or perhaps a little above" its theoretical potential.
The FOMC members generally agreed that that was a likely prospect, the minutes show.
Members expected consumer spending to pick up after a summer decline, "though probably to a pace appreciably below that in the first half of the year."
Strong gains in employment and income, plus increased household wealth as a result of stock and bond market gains, should translate into higher spending ahead, the members said.
However, an increase in consumer debt burdens would tend to restrain any improvement in the consumer sector, the members said.
